name: DHT11 Temp & Humidity (3-pin module)
desc: Measures temperature (0–50°C) and humidity. The 3-pin module version already has the resistor it needs built in.
variantNote: 3-pin module: plug and play, no extra resistor.

name: DHT11 Temp & Humidity (bare 4-pin)
desc: The same DHT11 sensor without a board around it. It needs a 10kΩ resistor between VCC and DATA to work.
variantNote: Bare 4-pin: needs a 10kΩ pull-up resistor; pin 3 is not connected.

name: DHT22 / AM2302 Temp & Humidity
desc: A more accurate version of the DHT11 (±0.5°C, full 0–100% humidity, works below zero). Slower: one reading every 2 seconds.

name: DS18B20 Waterproof Temp Probe
desc: A sealed metal temperature probe on a cable (-55 to 125°C). Dip it in water, soil or coffee. Several probes can share one data pin.
note: Needs a 4.7kΩ pull-up resistor between DATA and VCC.

name: HC-SR04 Ultrasonic Distance (5V)
desc: Measures distance (2–400 cm) with sound pulses, like a bat. Great for parking sensors, robots and "don't come closer" alarms.
variantNote: Classic 5V version: its ECHO pin outputs 5V.

warn.3.3: HC-SR04 ECHO sends 5V back. With a 3.3V board, add a voltage divider (1kΩ + 2kΩ) on ECHO, or use the 3.3V version (RCWL-1601).

name: Ultrasonic Distance 3.3V (RCWL-1601 / HC-SR04P)
desc: Same job and same 4 pins as the HC-SR04, but it runs happily on 3.3V too. The safe choice for ESP32 and Pico.
variantNote: 3.3V-friendly version: power it from the same voltage as your board.

name: HC-SR501 PIR Motion Sensor
desc: Detects people and animals moving nearby (up to ~7 m) by sensing body heat. Two little knobs set sensitivity and how long it stays on.
note: Give it about 1 minute to settle after power-up. Its output is 3.3V, which is safe for every board.

name: Photoresistor (LDR, bare)
desc: A tiny part whose resistance changes with light. Paired with a 10kΩ resistor it tells your board how bright or dark it is.
variantNote: Bare part: you build the divider with a 10kΩ resistor.

name: Light Sensor Module (LDR, AO/DO)
desc: A photoresistor on a small board with an analog output (AO) and an on/off output (DO) with a brightness knob. No extra resistor needed.
variantNote: Module: 3 or 4 pins, resistor and comparator already on board.

name: Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensor v1.2
desc: Push it into a plant pot to know when the soil is dry. Unlike cheap fork sensors it doesn't rust away.
note: Lower reading = wetter soil. Keep the electronics at the top dry.

name: MPU-6050 Accelerometer + Gyro (GY-521)
desc: Senses tilt, shaking and rotation. Use it for motion controls, step counters or a self-balancing robot.

name: BMP280 Pressure + Temperature (3.3V)
desc: Measures air pressure and temperature, which is enough to estimate altitude or spot incoming weather changes.

warn.5: BMP280 is a 3.3V-only board: wire VCC to 3.3V, never 5V. With a 5V Arduino it usually works over I2C, but a level shifter is the safe choice.

name: BME280 Temp + Humidity + Pressure (3.3V)
desc: Like the BMP280 but also measures humidity. A mini weather station in one chip.
note: Many cheap "BME280" listings are really BMP280s (no humidity). The chip on a real BME280 is square; on a BMP280 it is rectangular.

warn.5: BME280 (purple 6-pin board) is 3.3V-only: wire VCC to 3.3V, never 5V. With a 5V Arduino, a level shifter is the safe choice.

name: KY-038 Sound Sensor (mic module)
desc: A microphone module that detects loud sounds like claps and knocks. Good for clap switches, not good enough for recording audio.

name: MQ-2 Gas / Smoke Sensor
desc: Smells smoke and flammable gases (LPG, propane). Fun for experiments, but it is NOT a certified safety alarm.
note: It gets warm on purpose. Let it heat up for a few minutes before trusting readings.

warn.3.3: MQ-2 needs 5V power, and its analog output can reach 5V. Use a voltage divider (e.g. 10kΩ + 20kΩ) before a 3.3V board's analog pin.

name: TCRT5000 IR Line Sensor
desc: Shines invisible infrared light and checks what bounces back, so it can tell a black line from a white floor. The heart of line-following robots.

name: IR Flame Sensor Module
desc: Spots the infrared glow of a flame (a lighter or candle) from up to ~1 m. For experiments only, not a real fire alarm.

name: Water Level Sensor (exposed traces)
desc: A strip with metal lines that reads higher the more of it is under water. Handy for rain detectors and tank-level warnings.
note: The traces corrode if powered all the time. Power it from a board pin and switch it on only while reading.

name: MAX30102 Heart Rate & SpO2 Sensor
desc: Shines red and infrared light through your fingertip to estimate pulse and blood oxygen. A fun experiment, not a medical device.
note: Not a medical device. Rest your finger gently: pressing hard ruins the reading.

warn.5: Many MAX30102 boards pull I2C up to 1.8V or 3.3V. They often work with 5V boards, but a 3.3V board (ESP32/Pico) is the safer match.

name: AHT20 Temperature & Humidity (I2C)
desc: A small, accurate and fast temperature/humidity sensor that talks I2C: a modern upgrade over the DHT11.

name: SHT31 Temperature & Humidity (I2C)
desc: A precise Swiss-made sensor (±0.3°C) for weather stations and incubators.

name: BH1750 Light Sensor (lux)
desc: Measures light in real lux units, like a photographer's light meter, over I2C.

name: VEML7700 Ambient Light Sensor
desc: A very sensitive lux sensor that works from moonlight to bright sun.

name: TCS34725 Color Sensor (RGB)
desc: Reads the color of objects in red/green/blue values, with its own white LED. Sort candies by color!

name: TCS3200 Color Sensor (frequency output)
desc: An older color sensor that outputs a frequency for each color filter; needs 4 control pins.

name: APDS-9960 Gesture & Proximity Sensor
desc: Detects hand swipes (up/down/left/right), proximity and color. Wave to control your gadget!

warn.5: APDS-9960 boards are 3.3V only: power from 3.3V. Its I2C pins are 3.3V; a level shifter is the safe choice with 5V boards.

name: VL53L0X Laser Distance Sensor (ToF)
desc: Measures distance (up to ~1.2 m) with an invisible, eye-safe laser pulse. More precise and smaller than ultrasonic.
note: Class 1 laser: eye-safe in normal use.

name: VL53L1X Laser Distance Sensor (up to 4 m)
desc: The long-range version of the VL53L0X, measuring up to about 4 m.

name: TF-Luna LiDAR (0.2–8 m)
desc: A tiny LiDAR that measures up to 8 m, 100+ times a second. Great for robots and drones.

warn.5: TF-Luna's serial pins are 3.3V. Put a voltage divider (1kΩ + 2kΩ) on its RX when connecting a 5V board's TX.

name: JSN-SR04T Waterproof Ultrasonic Sensor
desc: An ultrasonic distance sensor with a sealed probe on a cable. Perfect for water tank levels (25–450 cm).
note: It can't see closer than about 25 cm.

warn.3.3: The JSN-SR04T ECHO pin outputs 5V. Use a voltage divider (1kΩ + 2kΩ) into a 3.3V board.

name: ADXL345 Accelerometer (GY-291)
desc: Senses tilt, taps and free-fall on 3 axes. Simpler than the MPU-6050 (no gyro).

name: QMC5883L Compass (GY-271)
desc: A digital compass that senses Earth's magnetic field to find north.
note: Many GY-271 boards sold as "HMC5883L" really carry a QMC5883L, which needs a different library. Check the chip marking.

name: BMP180 Pressure Sensor (GY-68)
desc: An older barometric pressure + temperature sensor. Its module has a regulator, so 5V is fine.

name: BME280 (5V-ready 4-pin board)
desc: A BME280 on a board with its own 3.3V regulator, so it can be powered from 5V. Same sensor, easier with an Uno.
variantNote: 4-pin board with a regulator: VCC can be 5V. I2C is pulled up to 3.3V, which works with most 5V boards.

name: BME680 Gas, Temp, Humidity & Pressure
desc: Four sensors in one: temperature, humidity, pressure and an air-quality (VOC gas) reading.
voltage: 3.3V (5V only on boards with a regulator; check yours)

name: AMG8833 Thermal Camera (8x8)
desc: A tiny 8x8-pixel thermal camera: see warm hands and hot cups as a heat map.

name: DS18B20 Temperature Sensor (TO-92 chip)
desc: The same digital DS18B20 thermometer as the probe, but as a small 3-leg chip for indoor use.
note: Looks like a transistor! Flat side facing you: GND, DATA, VDD. Needs a 4.7kΩ pull-up on DATA.

name: LM35 Analog Temperature Sensor
desc: Outputs 10 mV per °C. Read it with analogRead() and a little math.
note: Flat side facing you: +VS, VOUT, GND. Swapping + and GND makes it very hot!

name: TMP36 Analog Temperature Sensor
desc: A beginner-friendly analog thermometer: 10 mV per °C with a 500 mV offset, so it can read below zero.
note: Flat side facing you: +VS, VOUT, GND.

name: NTC Thermistor 10kΩ
desc: A resistor that changes with temperature. With a 10kΩ resistor it becomes a cheap thermometer.

name: MAX6675 + K-Type Thermocouple
desc: Measures very high temperatures (0–1024°C) with a metal thermocouple probe: ovens, grills, soldering irons.
note: Only the metal probe tip goes into the heat. Keep the module and wires away from hot surfaces.

name: MLX90614 Infrared Thermometer (GY-906)
desc: Measures an object's temperature without touching it, like a forehead thermometer.
note: Chips marked BAA are 3V, AAA are 5V. Many GY-906 boards add a regulator for 5V. Check yours.

name: HX711 Load Cell Amplifier
desc: Reads the tiny signal from a load cell so your board can weigh things in grams.

name: Load Cell 5 kg (bar type)
desc: A metal bar that bends a tiny amount under weight. Pair it with an HX711 to build a kitchen scale.
note: Wire colors: red E+, black E−, white A−, green A+ (check your seller's diagram).

name: Rain Sensor (FC-37 plate + module)
desc: A plate that detects raindrops, with a module giving analog (how wet) and digital (rain yes/no) outputs.
note: The plate corrodes if powered all the time. Power it from a pin only while reading.

name: Soil Moisture Sensor (resistive fork, FC-28)
desc: The cheap fork-shaped soil sensor. Works, but its metal legs rust within weeks if always powered.
note: Prefer the capacitive sensor for long-term use, or power this one only while measuring.

name: MAX4466 Microphone Amplifier
desc: A microphone with an adjustable amplifier, good enough to sample audio for VU meters and sound-reactive lights.

name: MAX9814 Microphone (auto gain)
desc: A microphone that automatically adjusts its volume, keeping quiet and loud sounds readable.

name: INMP441 I2S Digital Microphone
desc: A clean digital microphone for ESP32 and Pico: voice recording, speech experiments and spectrum displays.

warn.5: INMP441 needs I2S and 3.3V power, which the Uno/Nano/Mega/Leonardo don't have. Use an ESP32 or Pico.

name: A3144 Hall Effect Sensor (magnet switch)
desc: Switches when a magnet comes close. Count wheel turns or detect a closed lid.
note: Needs a pull-up resistor (10kΩ) on its output, or use INPUT_PULLUP.

warn.3.3: A3144 needs at least 4.5V: power it from 5V, and pull its output up to 3.3V (or use INPUT_PULLUP), never to 5V.

name: MC-38 Magnetic Door/Window Sensor
desc: Two plastic blocks: a magnet and a reed switch. When the door opens they separate and the circuit breaks.
note: Wire it between a pin and GND and use INPUT_PULLUP.

name: SW-520D Tilt Switch (ball switch)
desc: A tiny tube with a metal ball: it closes when upright and opens when tilted.

name: SW-420 Vibration Sensor Module
desc: Detects shaking and knocks (with a sensitivity knob). Good for tamper alarms and knock locks.

name: NEO-6M GPS Module
desc: Receives satellite signals to tell your project its location, speed and the exact time.
note: Needs a clear view of the sky. The first position fix can take a few minutes outdoors.

warn.5: The GPS module's RX pin is 3.3V. Put a voltage divider (1kΩ + 2kΩ) on it from a 5V board's TX.

name: MQ-135 Air Quality Sensor
desc: Reacts to gases like ammonia, smoke and CO2-like pollutants: a rough "is the air stuffy?" meter.
note: It needs a long warm-up and gives relative (not exact) readings.

warn.3.3: MQ-135 needs 5V for its heater, and its analog output can reach 5V. Use a voltage divider into a 3.3V board.

name: MQ-7 Carbon Monoxide Sensor (demo)
desc: A CO-sensitive gas sensor for experiments. It is NOT a carbon monoxide alarm.
note: Accurate CO measurement needs special heater cycling. Never use it as a safety alarm.

warn.3.3: MQ-7 needs 5V for its heater and its output can reach 5V. Use a voltage divider into a 3.3V board.

name: GUVA-S12SD UV Light Sensor
desc: Measures ultraviolet light from the sun: build a UV index meter for sunny days.

name: ACS712 Current Sensor (5A)
desc: Measures how much current flows through a wire, so you can see how hungry a motor or LED strip is.
note: Beginner rule: low-voltage DC only (12V and below), never mains.

warn.3.3: ACS712 needs 5V and its output centers at 2.5V and can reach 5V. Use a voltage divider into a 3.3V board.

name: INA219 Current & Voltage Sensor (I2C)
desc: Precisely measures voltage (up to 26V) and current (up to 3.2A) over I2C: a digital power meter.
note: Low-voltage DC only.

name: Voltage Sensor Module (0–25V)
desc: A simple resistor divider board that lets your board measure up to 25V, like a battery's voltage.
note: DC only. Never connect it to mains.

warn.3.3: On a 3.3V board the module can only measure up to about 16.5V, because its output is 1/5 of the input.

name: IR Obstacle Sensor (FC-51)
desc: Detects objects 2–30 cm in front of it with infrared light. A cheap robot whisker.
note: Its output goes LOW when something is in front. Sunlight can confuse it.

name: AM312 Mini PIR Sensor
desc: A tiny motion sensor that runs on 3.3V or 5V. Easy to hide inside small gadgets.

name: RCWL-0516 Microwave Radar Motion Sensor
desc: Senses movement with microwaves, even through plastic cases and thin walls.

warn.3.3: RCWL-0516 needs at least 4V: power it from 5V (VIN). Its output is 3.3V, which is safe for your board.

name: Pulse Sensor (analog, green LED)
desc: A clip-on finger or earlobe pulse sensor that outputs your heartbeat as an analog wave.
note: Fun experiment, not a medical device.

name: Flex Sensor 2.2" (bend sensor)
desc: A strip whose resistance rises as it bends. Put it on a glove finger to control a robot hand!
note: Use it with a 10kΩ–47kΩ resistor as a voltage divider.

name: Force Sensor FSR402 (pressure pad)
desc: A pad whose resistance drops when pressed. Detect squeezes, steps or a cat on the sofa.

name: Water Flow Sensor (YF-S201)
desc: Counts how much water flows through a pipe using a spinning wheel and pulses.

warn.3.3: The YF-S201 sends 5V pulses when powered from 5V. Use a voltage divider into a 3.3V board.

name: Dust Sensor (Sharp GP2Y1014AU)
desc: Measures dust and smoke particles in the air with an infrared LED inside.
note: Its LED pin needs a 150Ω resistor and a 220µF capacitor (see its datasheet circuit).

warn.3.3: The dust sensor needs 5V and its analog output can reach about 3.7V. Use a voltage divider into a 3.3V board.
